title: 2.3 Natural and Human Induced Climate Change
description: Milankovitch cycles, solar output, volcanic aerosols, land use change and greenhouse gas emissions. Medium level.

questions.question: What does eccentricity refer to in the Milankovitch theory?
options: Together they confirm that the climate is changing
Afforestation, reforestation and forest management
Changes in the shape of Earth orbit around the Sun
Climate is measured over years; weather over a day
questions.correctAnswer: Changes in the shape of Earth orbit around the Sun

questions.question: What does obliquity refer to?
options: It stops sea level rise instantly
Changes in orbital shape
The wobbling of the axis
Changes in the tilt of Earth axis
questions.correctAnswer: Changes in the tilt of Earth axis

questions.question: What does precession refer to?
options: The speed of ocean currents
The wobbling of Earth axis of rotation
Ocean water cools the mantle into lava
Shelves are affected by seasonal waves
questions.correctAnswer: The wobbling of Earth axis of rotation

questions.question: How can volcanic eruptions cool Earth surface?
options: Africa and South America were once contiguous
They indicated identical present-day climates
It extends beneath part of the Atlantic Ocean
Sulfuric acid haze reflects incoming sunlight
questions.correctAnswer: Sulfuric acid haze reflects incoming sunlight

questions.question: What effect do sulfate and nitrate aerosols have?
options: The core is broken into moving plates
They increase infrared trapping
Replacing coal power with wind energy
They mainly reflect incoming sunlight

questions.question: What effect does soot have?
options: It reflects all sunlight
It readily absorbs sunlight
It forms sulfuric acid haze
It cools the stratosphere

questions.question: How does deforestation affect local climate in the Amazon?
options: A ridge forms on land; a rift forms only in the ocean
It reduces evaporative cooling and raises temperature
Mountain belts formed independently on each continent
Shelves reveal the true submerged edges of continents
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces evaporative cooling and raises temperature

questions.question: What is desertification?
options: Dark forests absorb more sunlight than snow, accelerating warming
The North American Plate includes western North Atlantic seafloor
It eases impacts but does not limit the underlying climate change
An increase in desert conditions from overgrazing and cultivation
questions.correctAnswer: An increase in desert conditions from overgrazing and cultivation

questions.question: How much warming does methane cause compared with an equal mass of carbon dioxide over 100 years?
options: About 21 times as much
About the same amount
About one twenty-first as much
About 100 times less

questions.question: How much lower would Earth temperature be without greenhouse gases?
options: About 3 degrees Celsius lower
About 33 degrees Celsius lower
About 100 degrees Celsius lower
About 10 degrees Celsius higher
